jobs.title: Case Manager RN - Per Diem
jobs.description:
Optum Insight is improving the flow of health data and information to create a more connected system. We remove friction and drive alignment between care providers and payers, and ultimately consumers. Our deep expertise in the industry and innovative technology empower us to help organizations reduce costs while improving risk management, quality and revenue growth. Ready to help us deliver results that improve lives? Join us to start  Caring. Connecting. Growing together.

The Case Manager
is responsible and accountable for coordination of patient services through an interdisciplinary process, which provides a clinical and psychosocial approach through the continuum of care. Through concurrent case management, patients will be assessed to determine appropriateness of admission, continued hospitalization, as well as appropriate level of care. Discharge planning will begin at the time of (or prior to) admission, and reassessed ongoing throughout the course of hospitalization. Quality and Risk Management issues will also be monitored and reported as appropriate. CM may be assigned to various units throughout the hospital or the Emergency Department.
Schedule:
Required to work one weekend shift every two weeks. Other days as needed.
NOTE:
Qualified candidates must live in the Boulder CO regional area and be willing to work onsite at a hospital facility (not a remote work-from-home position.
Primary Responsibilities:

The CM will be responsible for integrating the assessment of the need for post-hospital services and determination of an appropriate discharge plan for complex cases
Educates patient/family as to options/choices within the level of care determined to be appropriate. Initiates and ensures completion of all necessary paperwork
Facilitates completion of orders as required prior to transfer of patient to the next level of care in a timely manner so discharge is not delayed
Continuum of Care planning will emphasize education and collaboration with physicians, family members, clinical social workers, nursing staff, therapists and case managers from contracted payors when appropriate to determine discharge plan that will be of maximum benefit to the patient. Involve staff from the next level of care in the treatment plan as early as possible to promote continuity and collaboration
Reports all relevant information to the staff assuming responsibility in the next level of care
Employees are expected to comply with all regulatory requirements, including CMS and Joint Commission Standards
Knowledge of all applicable federal and state regulations. Demonstrates a working knowledge of managed care and Medicare health plans as well as reimbursement related to post-acute services within the continuum of care
Consults with physician section leaders for support in cases where continued stay is not appropriate, and case managers are unable to come to resolution by working with assigned physician
Responsible for communicating with the department director LOS and financial information, as well as issues that may affect the Continuum of Care process
All employees are expected to remain flexible to meet the needs of the hospital, which may include floating to other departments to assist as the patient's needs fluctuate
Reviews the patient plan of care with the multi-disciplinary team. Facilitates and participates in multi-disciplinary team care conferences for patients with complex problems. Communicates in the medical record and verbally with the team to coordinate interventions and facilitate continuity of care
Daily communication and collaboration with the patient care staff to provide continuous assessment, evaluation and continuum planning to assure the patient receives the appropriate level of care at the appropriate time
Coordinates patient care processes to achieve desired quality outcomes and identifies/controls inappropriate resource utilization
Facilitates patient and family education and promotes continuity of care to achieve optimal patient outcomes. Assures patient rights by offering a choice when appropriate

Professional Accountabilities:

Adheres to name badge/dress code compliance
Effectively solves problems and actively pursues resolution
Directly communicates with staff, physicians, patients and families in a professional and courteous manner
Role models leadership behavior through courtesy, respect and efficiency
Functions without direct supervision, utilizing time constructively and organizing assignments for maximum productivity. Arranges schedule to facilitate meeting with physicians for patient care rounds, team meetings and other opportunities to improve communication 

You'll be rewarded and recognized for your performance in an environment that will challenge you and give you clear direction on what it takes to succeed in your role as well as provide development for other roles you may be interested in.
Required Qualifications:

Registered Nurse (RN) with a current, active, unrestricted RN License in Colorado OR a Social Worker (either a Licensed Clinical Social Worker [LCSW] in Colorado or Master of Social Work [MSW] will qualify) or ability to obtain within 6 months of hire
2+ years of experience working as a clinician in an acute care setting with proficient knowledge of hospital workflows
Live in the Boulder CO regional area (this position is location based and not open to remote work)
Willing/able to work one weekend shift per two weeks and availability as needed

Preferred Qualifications:

Case management experience or certification
Knowledge or understanding of community resources, policies, and procedures
Solid clinical acumen with the ability to use sound judgment, deductive reasoning, and problem-solving skills
Demonstrates a high level of organization with the ability to stay focused on the detail
Demonstrates collaborative skills and ability to interact with people of diverse backgrounds
Solid written and verbal communication skills
Self-motivated and able to function in a fast-paced work environment
Meets and maintains quality and productivity standards
Solid working knowledge of Microsoft packages
Ability to learn and understand various clinical software applications
Proficient typing skills
Effectively solves problems and actively pursues resolution
Critical thinking and organizational skills

Pay is based on several factors including but not limited to local labor markets, education, work experience, certifications, etc. In addition to your salary, we offer benefits such as, a comprehensive benefits package, incentive and recognition programs, equity stock purchase and 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). No matter where or when you begin a career with us, you'll find a far-reaching choice of benefits and incentives. The hourly pay for this role will range from $29.00 to $52.00 per hour based on full-time employment. We comply with all minimum wage laws as applicable.

At UnitedHealth Group, our mission is to help people live healthier lives and make the health system work better for everyone. We believe everyone-of every race, gender, sexuality, age, location, and income-deserves the opportunity to live their healthiest life. Today, however, there are still far too many barriers to good health which are disproportionately experienced by people of color, historically marginalized groups, and those with lower incomes. We are committed to mitigating our impact on the environment and enabling and delivering equitable care that addresses health disparities and improves health outcomes - an enterprise priority reflected in our mission.

jobs.description:
✨ Senior Social Worker (Level 4) – Combine specialist clinical practice with meaningful leadership, mentoring and service development across CAMHS.

Remuneration
: $66.36 - $67.97 Per Hour + 12% Super + Salary Packaging

: Temporary Part Time until February 2027

: Social Worker Level 4

: 14

Lake Macquarie Site (1A Dudley Road, Charlestown NSW 2290)

Requisition ID
: REQ688308

Applications Close:
Thursday 24th September 2026

🌿About The Role

As a Senior Social Worker (Level 4) within CAMHS, you will work in partnership with another Senior Social Worker as part of a job-share arrangement, providing high-quality specialist assessment, therapeutic intervention, consultation, and clinical leadership to children, young people, and their families/carers experiencing significant mental health concerns.

The role combines direct clinical work with discipline-specific leadership responsibilities, including consultation, mentoring, education, supervision and support to clinicians within a multidisciplinary environment.

You will provide specialist patient-centred clinical advice to consumers, families/carers and healthcare professionals, contribute to service development and quality improvement initiatives, and support the capability and professional growth of Social Work staff across the HNE CAMHS network.

You will receive direct line management from the CAMHS Greater Newcastle Team Leader and work alongside an experienced multidisciplinary team including Social Workers, Psychologists, Occupational Therapists, Nurses, Dietitians and Child and Adolescent Psychiatrists.

The role includes regular professional supervision, discipline-specific mentoring, structured orientation and ongoing professional development opportunities. You will also have access to specialist consultation, peer support and district-wide Social Work leadership networks to support your ongoing growth as a senior clinician and leader.

📍Where You’ll Be Working

An exciting opportunity is available for an experienced Senior Social Worker (Level 4) to join our supportive and dynamic Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service (CAMHS) Greater Newcastle team on a temporary part-time basis for 6 months, working 14 hours per week. The successful applicant will work in a job-share arrangement with another Senior Social Worker (Level 4), providing continuity of senior Social Work expertise and leadership across the service.

This position is based with the Lake Macquarie CAMHS team at 1A Dudley Road, Charlestown, with occasional travel to other Greater Newcastle CAMHS locations during work hours as required. While operationally based within Greater Newcastle, this role also has district-wide responsibilities, supporting the development and growth of the Social Work workforce across Hunter New England CAMHS.

This is a unique opportunity to combine specialist child and adolescent mental health practice with district-wide professional leadership and workforce development, contributing to the future direction of Social Work within HNE CAMHS.

CAMHS is a specialist mental health service providing assessment, treatment and care coordination for children and young people aged 0–17 years and their families/carers across Hunter New England Local Health District (HNELHD). We work within a collaborative multidisciplinary environment, delivering individual, dyadic and family-based interventions to support young people experiencing complex and severe mental health difficulties.

Staff are supported through strong local governance structures and the broader CAMHS and Mental Health networks. The Senior Social Worker (Level 4) is a key leader within both the local team and the wider CAMHS Social Work network

What We Can Offer You

At Hunter New England Health, enjoy a career where you're challenged by interesting work and surrounded by spectacular locations. You'll contribute to the team enriching health in millions of ways every day. On top of this we also offer:

Supportive and collaborative team environment

Ongoing professional development opportunities across the administrative network

Career progression opportunities within NSW Health

Annual leave and paid parental leave for eligible employees

Essential Requirements

Must hold as a minimum a bachelor degree in social work which provides eligibility for membership of the Australian Association of Social Workers, or other qualification deemed equivalent by the employer.
Eligibility to drive in NSW and interstate and the willingness to travel in the course of employment.

If this sounds like you, we would love you to apply:

🧠 Extensive experience in conducting comprehensive psychosocial assessments and delivering evidence-based therapeutic interventions for children, young people and their families/carers navigating complex mental health presentations.

🤝 Highly developed interpersonal, consultation and conflict resolution skills, with a natural ability to build trusted, respectful and effective professional and therapeutic relationships.

💡 The ability to provide specialist clinical advice and expertise to service managers, contributing to clinical service delivery, practice development and responsive service redesign aligned with consumer and community needs.

🌟 Advanced clinical reasoning skills, with the confidence and capability to provide specialist clinical consultation, guidance and leadership within a collaborative multidisciplinary environment.

❤️ A genuine commitment to best-practice care, underpinned by evidence-based, trauma-informed, family-centred and culturally responsive approaches.

🔄 Flexibility, initiative and sound prioritisation skills, with the ability to navigate competing demands while contributing to service improvement and positive outcomes for consumers.

jobs.description:
THE POSITION

Step into a role that makes Pennsylvania’s outdoor spaces come alive! As the Outdoor Recreation and Interpretation Program Coordinator for the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, you help people discover new ways to explore nature. You guide programs that build outdoor skills, strengthen partnerships, and support lifelong learning. This position is perfect for someone who enjoys motivating others and creating meaningful outdoor experiences.

DESCRIPTION OF WORK

This position guides the development, coordination, and evaluation of statewide outdoor recreation and environmental education programs. The work strengthens public engagement, supports field staff, and ensures high-quality learning experiences across many initiatives. As a Outdoor Recreation and Interpretation Program Coordinator, you will perform the following duties:

Program Leadership: Lead statewide coordination, development, and evaluation of outdoor recreation and environmental education programs
Training Support: Develop and deliver training sessions, workshops, and lesson plans for field personnel and educators
Partnership Coordination: Work with agencies, schools, and organizations to advance recreation and education initiatives
Content Development: Create educational materials, virtual programs, and informational resources for public use
Program Evaluation: Assess program effectiveness, review reports, and recommend improvements to statewide initiatives
Technical Guidance: Provide expert assistance, interpret policies, and support field staff with program needs

Interested in learning more? Additional details regarding this position can be found in the position description .

Work Schedule and Additional Information:

Full-time employment
Work hours are 7:30 AM to 4:00 PM, Monday - Friday, with a 60-minute lunch.
Telework: You may have the opportunity to work from home (telework) part-time, 5 days in a 10 day pay period. In order to telework, you must have a securely configured high-speed internet connection and work from an approved location inside Pennsylvania. If you are unable to telework, you will have the option to report to the headquarters office in Harrisburg. The ability to telework is subject to change at any time. One year of experience as a Natural Resource Program Specialist 1 (Commonwealth job title or equivalent Federal Government job title, as determined by the Office of Administration) ; or
Three years of professional experience in natural resource management or natural resource education; and a bachelor's degree in natural resource management, parks and recreation, education, biology, forestry, ecology, geosciences, environmental sciences, or a closely related field ; or

jobs.title: PALM (Pacific Australia Labour Mobility) Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
Great at organising, coordinating and making things happen? Love working with people from different backgrounds? This could be the opportunity for you.

Hybrid role with flexible full-time working hours
Dynamic and rewarding opportunity with an industry leader
Diverse, people-focused role where no two days are the same
No previous PALM experience required – full training provided

Make a real difference to people's experience in Australia

At Flavorite, our people are at the heart of what we do.
We're looking for a highly organised, people-focused PALM Program Adviser to help coordinate and support our Pacific Australia Labour Mobility (PALM) Program across our Tatura, Katunga and Mansfield sites.

This is much more than an administration role. You'll coordinate everything from recruitment and arrivals through to accommodation, wellbeing, community connections and departures - helping ensure our PALM Team Members feel welcomed, supported and set up for success while living and working in Australia.

You'll work with people from a wide range of cultures and backgrounds, build relationships across our business and local communities, solve problems, coordinate multiple priorities and help continuously improve how we deliver our program.

You don't need previous PALM experience. We'll provide the training and support to help you understand the program and its requirements.

If you've built your experience in administration, coordination, operations, workforce planning, community services, People & Culture, recruitment, customer service or another fast-paced people-focused environment, we'd love to hear from you.

What you'll be doing

Working closely with our operational and People teams, and supporting one direct report, you'll help coordinate the day-to-day delivery of Flavorite's PALM Program, including:

Recruitment & mobilisation:
Coordinate PALM workforce planning and recruitment, working with internal teams, Labour Sending Units to ensure candidates meet Flavorite’s requirements and all PALM compliance obligations are met. Coordinate arrivals, onboarding and essential services setup, ensuring new PALM Team Members have a smooth and well-supported orientation
Administration, Budgeting & Reporting
: Maintain accurate records and complete required timely internal and government reporting.
Contribute to PALM workforce planning and budgeting processes by providing insights, data, and operational needs to inform strategic decisions
Pastoral (Wellbeing) Care:
Conduct regular group pastoral care/wellbeing check-ins with PALM Team Members in alignment with Government Deed obligations, ensuring worker wellbeing is actively monitored and supported.
Accommodation Oversight
: Regularly inspect and monitor worker accommodation to ensure it meets PALM & Flavorite standards and promptly action any maintenance or welfare issues.

Community Engagement:
Continue to build relationships with local services and community organisations to support inclusion and connection.
Healthcare Support:
Assist PALM Team Members to access healthcare and understand Medicare, appointments and health insurance processes.
Departure Planning:
Prepare & deliver smooth end-of-season transitions, including travel arrangements, final payments, and repatriation coordination, in accordance with PALM Scheme requirements.
Leadership Capability Building:
Collaborate with People Leaders to develop strategies, tools, and skills that enable them to better train, support, and engage with PALM Team Members throughout their employment.
Continuous improvement:
Champion a culture of continuous improvement by simplifying and streamlining PALM processes, using data and feedback to identify opportunities, improve the PALM experience, strengthen compliance and drive better outcomes for all.

What will help you thrive in this role?

We're interested in what you can bring to the role - not whether you've done this exact job before.

You might be an experienced administrator or coordinator ready for your next step, or you may come from operations, recruitment, community services, workforce coordination, People & Culture or another role where you've become known as the person who keeps things moving.

You'll ideally bring:

Great communication skills and a genuine ability to connect with people from different backgrounds
A collaborative approach and willingness to work across different teams, sites and communities
A practical, solutions-focused approach - you enjoy figuring things out and getting things done
Confidence managing multiple priorities and deadlines
Strong administration, coordination and organisational skills
Strong attention to detail and confidence maintaining accurate records
Confidence using Microsoft Office and learning new systems
Integrity, discretion and sound judgement
A current driver's licence, as regular travel to Katunga and Mansfield is part of the role
A current National Police Check, or willingness to obtain one

Most importantly, you'll enjoy working with people and contributing to a diverse, multicultural workplace.

Why Flavorite?

Flavorite is one of Australia's leading fresh produce businesses, and behind our produce is a diverse team of people who bring different experiences, cultures and perspectives to work every day.

This role gives you the opportunity to combine your administration and coordination strengths with meaningful, people-focused work.

You'll have variety, autonomy and the opportunity to build relationships across our sites and communities while helping shape a PALM Program that supports both our Team Members and our business.

If you're organised, approachable, curious and love bringing people and processes together, we'd love to hear from you.

Previous PALM Program experience is not required. If you have the transferable skills and enthusiasm to learn, we encourage you to apply.

Our Perks & Benefits

Retail Perks
: Save on hundreds of everyday items, including groceries, fuel, movie tickets, homewares, electronics and more through exclusive discounts.
Wellness Discounts:
Access a variety of offers to support your physical, mental, and financial well-being, plus helpful resources on topics like budgeting, saving for your first home, and improving sleep.
Lifestyle Benefits:
Enjoy savings on health insurance, gym memberships, superannuation, and home loans, with easy access to our wellness resources and discounts.
Fresh Produce Giveaways:
Regular team giveaways of fresh produce at our farm sites
Recognition & Rewards:
We celebrate service anniversaries, special milestones, and team achievements with recognition and rewards.
Community Involvement
: Get involved in our volunteering initiatives and give back to our community.

We’re growing. That means you can too.

We’re expanding beyond 100 hectares in the next five years and we’re growing careers just as fast. Whether you're upskilling, stepping up, or chasing new goals, we’re here to grow with you.

We’re Serious About Sustainability.

With over 30 years of growing experience, we set ourselves apart by our flavour and sustainability through our greenhouse-grown produce and our investment in cutting-edge technology.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Flavorite is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to providing a working environment that embraces and values diversity and inclusion.

jobs.description:
The best possible care
.

The best possible you
.

At Nexus Hospitals, we believe every patient deserves the quality and comfort of world-class care, right in their own community. We also believe that every team member deserves a life that keeps them at their best.

With a proud, growing network of 21 specialist hospitals across Australia, we offer the scale, stability and impact of a national healthcare leader, but with the tight-knit heart of a local team. By focusing on elective, day and short-stay surgeries, we provide our teams with a healthier work rhythm, so you can build a career you'll be proud of without sacrificing what matters most to you.

Join us and discover a workplace built for humans - where world-class care meets a world-class life.

About Our Hospital

Pacific Private Hospital specialises in elective surgery across:

Orthopaedics
Ophthalmology
Plastic Surgery
Mohs Surgery
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery
General Surgery
Gastroenterology & Hepatology

Our facility features 7 operating theatres and 8 inpatient beds
.

Following a recent expansion, our newly developed hospital provides a state-of-the-art environment designed to combine the capabilities of a conventional hospital with the efficiency and personalised experience of a day surgery facility.

Your Opportunity

We are seeking an experienced and motivated Administration Team Leader – Bookings to join our team.

This is a Full-time fixed term Maternity Leave relief
position with potential for ongoing employment -
November 2026 - September 2027

As a key member of our hospital, you will play an important role in ensuring the smooth coordination of theatre bookings and supporting an exceptional experience for patients, medical practitioners and our wider team.

This is a hands-on leadership role where your organisational skills, attention to detail and ability to build strong relationships will make a genuine difference every day.

With Respect And Collaboration, You Will

Manage theatre bookings: ensuring operating lists are accurate, complete and distributed within required timeframes.
Support administrative performance: Ensure documentation is accurately recorded and patient quotes are recorded and within timeframes. Liaise with health funds and complete checks
Build strong stakeholder relationships: Develop positive working relationships with Visiting Medical Officers, practice staff, patients, colleagues and other key stakeholders.

Lead, mentor and educate: Provide guidance, coaching and leadership to the team.
Keep patient safety central: Maintain clear communication with the team and respond proactively to risks, changes or concerns.
Champion continuous improvement, contributing to a culture of safety, quality, efficiency and genuinely patient-centred care.

Who We’re Looking For

You are a compassionate and dedicated professional who pairs administrative excellence with a genuinely warm, patient-first approach. You thrive in a collaborative, down-to-earth environment and take real pride in the high standard of care you provide.

new_jobs.title: Program Manager- Homelessness, Mental Health & AOD
new_jobs.description:
Lead. Inspire. Make a difference.

CatholicCare is growing, and this is an exciting opportunity to join our Homelessness service at an important time in its development.

We’re looking for a Program Manager who brings strong knowledge of homelessness, mental health and AOD, a passion for quality practice and the ability to support and inspire a team of Caseworkers, providing practice leadership, supervision and mentoring while helping shape a strong, connected and outcomes-focused service.

This is more than a team leadership role. It’s an opportunity to influence practice, build capability and help strengthen the way we support people experiencing homelessness and mental health challenges.

This is a permanent full-time role based in Hornsby and requires the incumbent to be office based for the first 6 months. After successful completion of the probation period, there will be an option to work from home.

About The Role

As a Program Manager, you’ll provide day-to-day practice leadership to a team supporting individuals and families experiencing homelessness and housing instability, often facing intersecting challenges including mental health, alcohol and other drug (AOD) issues, family violence, and other complex needs.

You’ll bring your specialist knowledge to complex situations, helping the team develop practical, person-centered responses that build stability, safety and wellbeing.

You will work closely alongside other Program Managers within our Homelessness portfolio. Through collaboration, shared leadership and a commitment to continuous improvement, you will contribute to the development of best practice approaches that support high-quality service delivery for people experiencing homelessness and complex, intersecting needs.

Working closely with internal and external stakeholders, you’ll help connect people with the right services and strengthen pathways across the homelessness, mental health and community services sectors. You’ll also play an important role in building a positive team culture where Caseworkers feel supported, challenged and confident in their practice.

What You’ll Do

Lead, supervise and mentor a team of 7 Caseworkers, including providing clinical/practice supervision.
Lead the day-to-day operations of our drop-in centre, supporting high-quality service delivery, positive client outcomes, continuous improvement and a safe, inclusive environment for all visitors.
Provide specialist guidance and support around complex homelessness and mental health presentations.
Support the team to deliver high-quality, trauma-informed and strengths-based casework.
Work alongside Caseworkers to develop practical interventions that improve housing stability, wellbeing and client outcomes.
Build strong referral pathways and relationships across homelessness, mental health, health and community services.
Develop and maintain effective partnerships with government and non-government organisations.
Support the team with risk assessment, crisis response and complex decision-making.
Promote reflective practice, professional development and continuous improvement.
Ensure practice aligns with program requirements and the Human Services Outcomes Framework.
Monitor and report on outcomes to ensure the service is achieving meaningful results.
Foster a positive, collaborative and high-performing team culture.

What You’ll Bring

We’re looking for someone who combines strong people leadership with genuine specialist knowledge of homelessness and mental health.

Tertiary qualifications in Social Work, Psychology, Counselling or a related discipline.
Experience leading, supervising or providing practice/clinical leadership to a team.
Strong knowledge and practical experience working within the homelessness and/or mental health sectors.
Experience supporting people experiencing complex and intersecting challenges.
A strong understanding of trauma-informed, strengths-based and person-centred practice.
Confidence working with complex risk, crisis situations and challenging presentations.
Strong assessment, problem-solving and professional decision-making skills.
The ability to build trusted relationships with clients, colleagues and external stakeholders.
Strong networking, advocacy and partnership-building skills.
A genuine commitment to improving outcomes for people experiencing homelessness and mental health challenges.

Why CatholicCare?

This is an exciting time to join CatholicCare.

We’re a growing service with strong leadership, a supportive team environment and a genuine focus on making a difference.

As a Program Manager, you’ll have the support and opportunity to make your mark: developing your team, influencing practice and contributing to the continued growth of our Homelessness service.

You’ll Also Have Access To

Not-for-profit salary packaging - increase your take-home pay by packaging a portion of your salary tax-free.
Regular reflective and practice supervision.
Ongoing training and professional development opportunities.
Employee Assistance Program providing free and confidential counselling and support.
CatholicCare Day - an additional paid leave day at the end of the year.
Flexible work arrangements.
A supportive, respectful and inclusive workplace.
Opportunities to grow your career within a growing CatholicCare service.

Ready for Your Next Opportunity?

If you’re looking for a leadership role where you can use your specialist knowledge, develop a team and help shape a growing service, we’d love to hear from you.

Bring your expertise in homelessness and mental health and join CatholicCare as we continue to grow our impact in the community.

THE POSITION

Join the Torrance State Hospital team as a Social Worker 1 and make a real difference in the lives of patients who need consistent, high-quality care and support. This role is currently assigned to work in our civil program supporting individuals who are generally admitted to TSH based on referrals from community in-patient psychiatric hospitalization. You will work directly with patients, families, community groups, and external agencies to provide the full range of social work services for an assigned caseload of adults in our care. Apply now for the chance to build a career that changes lives every day!

DESCRIPTION OF WORK

This role focuses on supporting a patient population through social work services in an in-patient setting. Work involves direct contact with individuals and their families, communication with a variety of external agencies, and consultation with other professional disciplines to ensure each person receives benefits and services in line with treatment plan. As a Social Worker 1, you will perform the following duties:

Clinical Interviews: Conduct interviews with individuals and their families, legal guardians, and external agency representatives to gather and update information
Assessment Work: Identify and determine each individual’s strengths and weaknesses as well as their need and eligibility for social work services
Care Planning: Participate in interdisciplinary meetings to develop and implement comprehensive treatment plans and individual goal planning
Case Management: Document progress, confer with other care providers and agencies, and respond to a variety of correspondence on patient care and related circumstances
Family Communication: Advise families and guardians of treatment progress and encourage their involvement
Legal Responsibilities: Complete mental health petitions for involuntary commitment, assist patients in legal matters, and testify at hearings
